A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LVAgent work and contain complete main texts and appendices. Their equations, figures, tables, and prompts can be reliably matched across relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original results on four video-understanding benchmarks, inference-efficiency measurements, and component and configuration ablations in Tables 1–7 and Figure 7.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds aggregate efficiency accounting and four-agent evaluation results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The Selection, Perception, Action, and Reflection procedures, retrieval rules, stopping mechanism, and prompts remain unchanged. Appendix B documents selected teams and evaluates four agents without changing the proposed three-agent default.

E1.justification: Both versions use EgoSchema, LongVideoBench, MLVU, and VideoMME, including the same subtitle conditions. LongVR retains the same five source datasets and 82,015 instances. The appendix additions introduce no new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–7 are retained. CLIP and LongCLIP remain evaluated in Table 5 despite their names disappearing from its accompanying discussion. The four-agent addition is a configuration ablation of LVAgent.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 adds evaluation of a four-agent configuration, extending the previously reported configurations of up to three agents. Existing splits, decoding settings, sampling rules, and retriever-training settings remain unchanged. Appendix B.1's task-specific team lists are newly disclosed settings, not demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 extends the agent-count analysis to four agents and measures its accuracy–latency tradeoff. Appendix B.2 adds a cost breakdown covering fine-tuning, preselection, and evaluation. Existing component, retrieval, discussion, threshold, and collaboration-round analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, explicit random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added appendix results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 and Section 4.3 revise LVAgent's reported latency from 15.1 to 33.6 seconds without explaining the cause. Appendix B.2 adds aggregate timing results; B.3 adds four-agent scores of 83.0 on EgoSchema, 80.1 on LongVideoBench, 84.1 on MLVU, and 81.8/86.5 on VideoMME without/with subtitles, at 38.7 seconds. The headline margin changes from 14.3% to 13.3%, while Table 1 and existing ablation accuracy values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), including pseudo-label accuracy, retrieval similarity, agent scoring, and information updates, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion correct the claimed LongVideoBench margin from 14.3% to 13.3%, consistent with the retained 80.0 versus GPT-4o's 66.7 in Table 1. The central novelty, collaboration, and benchmark-superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 adds an explicit accuracy–efficiency rationale for retaining three agents despite testing four. Section 4.4 removes the attribution of ASP-CLIP's advantage to superior temporal alignment, while retaining its reported advantage and the other mechanism interpretations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link in the abstract and task-specific agent identities and sizes in Appendix B.1. Appendix B.2 newly discloses the 95M-parameter fine-tuning setup, three-hour training time, and preselection/evaluation workload and timing breakdowns. Existing hyperparameters, hardware information, data recipes, and prompt templates remain.

R1.justification: The distinct cited works and research-positioning arguments are retained. Reference changes update publication metadata and authorship, reorder entries, and remove a duplicate LongVA reference; they do not introduce a new research relationship.

P1.justification: The abstract and portions of Sections 4.3–4.4 are shortened, with limited wording and bibliographic cleanup. A new experimental-details Appendix B shifts the existing prompts section to Appendix C. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves from page 5 to page 7, Figure 6 moves from page 6 to page 5, and existing plots and surrounding text are resized or reflowed. All seven figures and nine tables are retained without substantive graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves consistency by aligning the headline LongVideoBench margin with Table 1, and improves reproducibility through explicit agent selections, a code-access link, and fuller cost accounting. The four-agent analysis supports the default configuration's efficiency rationale. These are useful but limited gains: core accuracy evidence is unchanged, and the substantial latency revision remains unexplained.
